codes.label: Delivery Method/Project Structure Clause
codes.definition: The contractual framework establishing the overall project delivery structure (design-bid-build, design-build, CM, IPD multiparty, EPC/turnkey) and the resulting allocation of design, procurement and construction responsibility.
codes.memo: Combines T1's comparative delivery-method codes (DBB unsuitability, DB as integrator, IPD as optimal, EPC/turnkey single-point responsibility, CM-GC options), T5's 'Project Delivery Method Choice' category, T7's procurement/delivery selection category, T9's 'collaborative delivery methods as relational mechanisms', and T12's 'Delivery System Influence' code. Needed because the choice of underlying delivery model, as expressed or assumed in a standard form, fundamentally frames how MMC/prefab issues are addressed contractually.

codes.label: Early Contractor/Manufacturer Involvement Provisions
codes.definition: Clauses establishing mechanisms (ECI, two-stage tendering, preconstruction services agreements, nominated supplier/strategic partnering terms) that bring contractors, fabricators or manufacturers into the design process before final pricing.
codes.memo: Merges T1's two-stage/ECI category, T7's 'Contractual Mechanisms for Early Involvement' category, T9's 'Early Involvement and Design-Phase Collaboration', and related codes from T5 and T12 on PCSAs and early engagement. Central to whether a contract structurally permits the early design input MMC requires.

codes.label: Design Freeze and Late-Change Consequence Clause
codes.definition: Provisions setting deadlines for design finalization prior to fabrication and specifying the cost/schedule consequences and approval processes for changes made after that point.
codes.memo: Combines T2's 'Late Design Changes in Off-site/Modular Fabrication', T7's 'Design Freeze Timing and Consequences' category, T8's 'design freeze and standardization tensions', T9's 'Design freeze and change order limitations', T12's 'Design Freeze Requirements Conflicting with Traditional Practice', and T13's related design-stage codes. Needed because contracts must formally embed the earlier design lock-in that off-site manufacturing demands.

codes.label: Definition of Work/Products Scope for Off-Site Components
codes.definition: Clause(s) defining 'Work', 'Products', materials and equipment to determine whether prefabricated modules and off-site-manufactured components are unambiguously covered.
codes.memo: Combines T2, T3 and T5 codes on 'Ambiguity in contractual definition of Products/modules' and related sub-codes. A discrete drafting issue distinguishable from payment mechanics, since it affects insurance, risk and payment coverage simultaneously.

codes.label: Progress/Final Payment and Certification for Off-Site Fabrication
codes.definition: Payment clauses (progress payment, certification for payment, final payment) evaluated for their fit with off-site manufacture, including milestone payment for manufactured-but-undelivered/uninstalled modules.
codes.memo: Merges T2's 'Payment Mechanisms Unsuited to Off-site Fabrication', T3's 'Standard Contract Payment Clause Gaps for MOC' category, T5's 'CCDC payment clause misalignment' and 'advance/off-site payment provisions', and T6 cash-flow codes. This is one of the most concrete, frequently cited clause-level gaps in the literature.

codes.label: Retention and Liquidated Damages Provisions
codes.definition: Standard retention holdback and liquidated damages clauses assessed for their fit with off-site production schedules and manufacturer risk exposure.
codes.memo: Drawn from T5's 'Retention and liquidated damages misalignment' code; kept separate from general payment code because retention/LDs raise distinct amendment practices in MMC contracts.

codes.label: Variation/Change Order Valuation and Scope-Limitation Clause
codes.definition: Provisions defining how variations are valued, limiting the scope of instructable changes, and specifying (or omitting) a contractor's right to decline variations.
codes.memo: Combines T2's 'Variation Valuation and Scope-Limitation Clauses', T5's corresponding category, and T11's ML-based classification of particular-conditions modifying change procedures. Distinct from design-freeze code because it addresses the mechanics of pricing/limiting change rather than timing.

codes.label: Value Engineering Benefit-Sharing Clause
codes.definition: Clause governing how cost savings from contractor-proposed value engineering/efficiency proposals are shared between owner and contractor.
codes.memo: From T2 and T5 'Value Engineering Benefit-Sharing' codes; kept discrete as it drives contractor incentive to propose prefabrication-enabling efficiencies.

codes.label: Differing Site Conditions and Force Majeure Clause
codes.definition: Provisions allocating risk for unforeseen physical site conditions and force majeure events, assessed for relevance where fabrication is decoupled from site.
codes.memo: From T2's 'Differing Site Conditions and Force Majeure' code; retained as a distinct standard clause type not eliminated by modularization.

codes.label: Changes in Law Clause
codes.definition: Provision (or absence thereof) addressing compensation/adjustment when applicable law changes during the contract term.
codes.memo: From T2 and T5 'Changes in Law' codes, highlighted because its absence forces reliance on informal claims rather than structured variation mechanisms.

codes.label: Risk Allocation Fairness and Disclaimer Clauses
codes.definition: General-conditions provisions and disclaimer language that transfer unforeseen or unpredictable risk unilaterally to one party (typically the contractor).
codes.memo: Merges T2's 'Unfair Risk Transfer', 'Risk-Party Matching Principle', T5's 'General conditions as principal risk-allocation instrument', 'Unilateral drafting', 'Disclaimer/risk-transferring clauses', and T8's parallel code. Core to assessing whether standard forms fairly allocate MMC-specific risks.

codes.label: General Conditions vs Particular Conditions Amendment Practice
codes.definition: How particular/supplementary conditions modify, clarify or unbalance the risk allocation set by the general conditions, including employer-driven unfavorable amendments.
codes.memo: Combines T2's 'Modification of Standard Forms Introducing Risk' (with sub-codes), T5's corresponding codes, and T11's ML classification of particular-conditions functions. Distinct code because amendment practice is a recurring, methodologically studied phenomenon.

codes.label: Transportation, Storage and Transit Insurance Clause
codes.definition: Clauses addressing lead-time, transport/lifting limitations, storage, and insurance coverage for modules/components between factory and site.
codes.memo: Merges T2's 'Lead-Time, Transport, and Logistics Risk Clauses', T3's 'Proposed Contractual Additions for MOC Payment' (insurance), T6's transportation/logistics risk category, T8's transportation/logistics code, and T13's cross-jurisdictional logistics code. A distinctive MMC-specific clause cluster absent from conventional contracts.

codes.label: Quality Assurance, Certification and Inspection Regime Clause
codes.definition: Contractual mechanisms specifying manufacturer self-certification, third-party/factory certification, mock-up approval and inspection processes for off-site components.
codes.memo: Draws on T8's certification/compliance category (self-certification, third-party certification, regulatory scoring), T7's mock-up/inspection QA code, and T6's mock-up code. Needed to evaluate how contracts embed compliance assurance for manufactured components.

codes.label: Chain of Custody and Component Traceability Clause
codes.definition: Provisions requiring tracking/identification technologies and documented responsibility transfer for components moving through the fabrication-to-installation supply chain.
codes.memo: From T8's 'Traceability, Chain of Custody' category; kept separate from QA/certification since it addresses supply-chain documentation rather than compliance standards per se.

codes.label: BIM/Digital Model Authorship, Ownership and Licensing Clause
codes.definition: Provisions clarifying ownership, authorship and licensing of BIM/digital model data, and whether 2D drawings or 3D models constitute the binding contract document.
codes.memo: Merges T5's BIM/DfMA category (model authorship, 2D vs 3D binding, software mandates), T8's parallel codes, and T11's 'Digital Model–Contract Text Interoperability' category. A distinct digital-fabrication contracting issue.

codes.label: Liability Allocation for Digital Fabrication and Design-Model Defects
codes.definition: Clause-level allocation of liability between designer, general contractor and fabricator for defects traceable to upstream digital models versus downstream fabrication.
codes.memo: Combines T5's 'Liability uncertainty in digital fabrication workflows' (with sub-codes), T8's 'Digital Fabrication, BIM and Liability Allocation' category. Distinguished from general risk-allocation code by its specific digital-fabrication liability chain focus.

codes.label: IPD/Multiparty Agreement and Shared Risk-Reward Mechanisms
codes.definition: Contractual features unique to Integrated Project Delivery and alliance-style agreements: multiparty signature, shared risk/reward pools, joint governance and target-cost/pain-gain sharing.
codes.memo: Merges T2's 'IPD Contractual Mechanisms', T5's 'Comparative analysis of standard IPD contract forms', T9's IPD/alliancing category, T1's 'IPD as optimal for total integration', and T3's 'Relational Contracting and Pain-Gain Sharing'. A distinct standard-form category (e.g., CCDC30) warranting its own code.

codes.label: Suspension and Termination Provisions
codes.definition: Clauses governing notice periods, discretion and consequences for suspension or termination of the contract, assessed for ambiguity/asymmetry.
codes.memo: From T2's 'Suspension and Termination Ambiguity' sub-code under IPD mechanisms; retained separately since it applies across delivery types, not only IPD.

codes.label: Liability Allocation Among Multiple Contracting Parties
codes.definition: General clauses defining liability boundaries among owner, designer, contractor, manufacturer and subcontractors, particularly in multiparty or fragmented arrangements.
codes.memo: From T2's 'Liability Allocation Clarity' sub-code and related fragmentation-liability material in T13; kept distinct from digital-fabrication-specific liability code (P17) as a broader clause category.

codes.label: Dispute Resolution, Claims and Extension-of-Time Handling
codes.definition: Provisions governing claim submission, EOT requests, tiered dispute resolution mechanisms and their administration.
codes.memo: Merges T2's 'Extension of Time (EOT) Claim Handling', 'Causal Chains and Co-occurrence of Dispute Factors', 'Litigation-Based Evidence', and IPD's 'tiered dispute resolution' feature. Needed to examine how contract mechanics for handling claims interact with MMC-specific disruptions.

codes.label: Contract Drafting Clarity, Readability and Consistency
codes.definition: The linguistic/structural quality of contract text—jargon, sentence complexity, visual aids, internal contradictions—as it affects interpretability and dispute risk.
codes.memo: Merges T2's 'Contract Document Quality and Completeness' category, T5's 'Readability and Drafting Quality' category, and T11's 'Contract Readability and Drafting Quality' category plus NLP-detectable ambiguity/contradiction codes. A cross-cutting drafting-quality lens applicable when coding any CCDC clause.

codes.label: Communication and Collaboration Protocol Clauses
codes.definition: Contract terms mandating communication turnaround (RFI/submittal timelines), data-sharing protocols, and collaborative decision-making structures between offsite and onsite parties.
codes.memo: Combines T2's 'Lack of Contractual Communication/Collaboration Provisions', T7's coordination-tools codes, and T9's 'Communication, Information-Sharing and Digital Collaboration Protocols' category. Needed because absence of such clauses is repeatedly cited as a dispute driver in MMC/prefab projects.

codes.label: Subcontract Flow-Down and Supply Chain Risk Transfer
codes.definition: Provisions governing how risk, cost and obligations flow down from general contractor to subcontractors, suppliers and manufacturers, including power asymmetries and upstream risk transfer.
codes.memo: Merges T6's 'Risk and Responsibility Allocation in Supply/Delivery Contracts' category, T9's 'Supply Chain and Multi-Actor Coordination' category, T10's 'Financial Risk Allocation Across the Supply Chain', T12's subcontractor repositioning category, and T13's risk/responsibility allocation category. Essential for evaluating how standard forms treat the fragmented MMC supply chain.

codes.label: Payment Security and Financial Guarantee Instruments
codes.definition: Clauses providing for bonds, letters of credit, bank guarantees, back-to-back payment terms, or other instruments securing cash flow and non-performance risk.
codes.memo: From T2's 'Payment-Security and Risk-Sharing Instruments' and T6's 'Financial risk-management clauses (guarantees, dual-sourcing)'. A discrete clause type addressing the front-loaded capital exposure unique to off-site manufacture.

codes.label: Automated/Smart Contract Payment and Penalty Enforcement Provisions
codes.definition: Contractual or supplementary provisions enabling blockchain/smart-contract-based automated payment, real-time incentive/penalty enforcement, and their governance limitations regarding change orders.
codes.memo: Merges T3's 'Smart Contract Implementation of Payment and Penalty Clauses' category, T4's technical architecture and limitations categories, and T11's 'Automated/Self-Executing Contract Mechanisms' category. Distinct code needed to evaluate how (or whether) CCDC clauses could interface with such automation and its governance gaps.

codes.label: Inflation and Price Escalation Adjustment Clause
codes.definition: Provisions (or their absence) allowing price adjustment for material/labour cost inflation, and use of off-site bulk procurement as a hedging strategy.
codes.memo: From T3's and T10's 'Inflation and Price-Volatility Risk Allocation' categories. A discrete, quantifiable clause-level gap identified via CCDC-14 stipulated-price analysis.

codes.label: Regulatory Compliance and Code/Standards Reference Clause
codes.definition: Clauses requiring compliance with applicable building codes, modular-specific standards, and government mandates, and addressing gaps where such codes/standards do not yet exist for MMC.
codes.memo: Merges T1's 'Legislative, policy and standards gaps', T8's 'Gaps in legislative frameworks and codes for MMC', T10's government incentive/mandate codes, and T13's 'Regulatory and Code Gaps' code. Needed to check whether contracts reference or accommodate evolving regulatory frameworks for MMC.

codes.label: Labour and Union Provisions Affecting Off-Site Work Allocation
codes.definition: Contractual or side-agreement provisions addressing labour union jurisdiction, work-hour allocation, and human-robot collaboration in the shift of work off-site.
codes.memo: From T6's and T9's 'Labor, Union, and Workforce Considerations' categories and T12's 'Labor Union Dynamics' category. Not a typical CCDC clause but relevant as a gap/negotiated-amendment area to check for in project-specific conditions.

codes.label: Delivery Schedule Deviation Incentive/Penalty Mechanism
codes.definition: Clauses (static or dynamic) allocating cost and responsibility for deviations between planned and actual component delivery/production schedules, including reward-penalty structures.
codes.memo: Merges T3's 'Component Delivery Schedule Risk and Compensation Mechanisms' category, T6's 'Just-in-Time Delivery and Schedule Coordination' category, and T4's incentive/penalty allocation category. A key MMC-specific scheduling-risk clause type distinct from general LDs (P6).

codes.label: Product-Based/Framework and Serial Contracting Structures
codes.definition: Contractual models moving away from single-project agreements toward long-term framework, serial-tendering or product-warranty-style contracts suited to repeatable manufactured products.
codes.memo: From T1's 'Product-Based and Non-Traditional Delivery Models' category; a novel contract-structure concept the literature proposes as a gap-filler for standard forms like CCDC.

codes.label: Insurance and Warranty Coverage for Prefabricated Components
codes.definition: Provisions defining insurance coverage (including during transport/storage) and warranty/guarantee obligations specific to manufactured and prefabricated components.
codes.memo: Combines T5's 'Lack of contractual clarity on guarantees and insurance for DfMA', T8's 'Insurance and lending mechanisms', and T13's insurance-adjacent codes. Distinguished from transportation clause (P13) by focus on coverage/warranty terms rather than logistics scheduling.

codes.label: Contractor/Manufacturer Qualification and Selection Criteria
codes.definition: Provisions or procurement criteria governing how contractors, fabricators and manufacturers are prequalified or selected, including alternatives to lowest-bid selection.
codes.memo: From T2's 'Lowest-Bid Contractor Selection' and T1's 'Feasibility scoring and selection tools'; relevant for evaluating tender/procurement-stage contract documents.

codes.label: Vertical Integration/Single-Entity Contracting Model
codes.definition: Contractual recognition (or non-recognition) of business models where design, manufacture and construction are delivered by a single integrated entity, redefining traditional party roles.
codes.memo: From T1's 'Vertical integration/single-firm delivery models', T7's 'Vertical integration as an alternative', and T9's 'Reduced actor count via integrated supplier-builder systems'. Relevant because standard forms assume separate parties that vertical integration collapses.

codes.label: Scope of Work, Roles and Responsibilities Definition Clause
codes.definition: Provisions clearly (or unclearly) defining scope of work, stakeholder roles, and references to multiple manufacturers/suppliers in DfMA and prefabrication contexts.
codes.memo: From T5's 'Unclear scope, roles, and responsibilities in DfMA contracts' and 'Lack of reference to multiple manufacturers', plus T13's related fragmentation codes. A foundational drafting-quality issue distinct from readability (P22), focused on substantive completeness rather than language.
